outcome: Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes after birth
cohort: 731 pregnant women with a BMI ≥ 30 kg/m(2) at the first prenatal care visit, compared to 3,161 women with a BMI between 18.5 kg/m(2) and 24.9 kg/m(2)
finding: Pre-pregnancy obesity was associated with older age, hyperglycemic disorders, hypertension syndrome, cesarean deliveries, fetal macrosomia, and fetal acidosis, but not with other perinatal outcomes such as duration of labor, Apgar scores, or congenital malformations.
mod_finding: Caesarean deliveries were more common in the obese group.
